description: Lychnion is an offline safety assistant for Japan. A phone or computer runs a small language model over installed, signed knowledge packages and shows sources and fixed official safety lines. Packages, maps and models come from signed catalogs over the internet, a base computer on the local Wi-Fi, a nearby phone, a USB stick or a headless node. A base also shares signed current facts such as shelter status.

trust_boundaries.boundary: `base-server`: in model if reachable by a client that can reach port 8642 or 8643. Reaching it from outside the local Wi-Fi or hotspot is itself a violation (§1.11 `lan-only-exposure`).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable by a client that can reach port 8642 or 8643

trust_boundaries.boundary: `base-client`: in model if reachable from a base's responses, an mDNS record, or a `lychnion://` link (`base`, `shelter`, `share`, `publisher`, `catalog`).

trust_boundaries.boundary: `facts`: in model if reachable from facts a base serves.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from facts a base serves

trust_boundaries.boundary: `device-data`: in model if data leaves the app sandbox: network, the system log, or shared storage.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: data leaving the app sandbox: network, system log, shared storage

trust_boundaries.boundary: **Statement to key.** Catalogs, sticks, bases, nearby phones and nodes also carry key statements. A statement changes trust only when a key the device already trusts for that publisher signed it.

assumes: **Platforms**: Android, iOS, macOS and Windows from one Flutter codebase. The headless node runs as a program or container on a server.
**Network**: a base needs a Wi-Fi that lets devices reach each other; the safest is a hotspot or router the shelter controls. The base page uses plain http.
**OS protections**: the app folder is private to the app (sandbox on macOS, iOS and Android; per-user AppData on Windows). The desktop publisher key relies on them.
**Files after install** are trusted. The app checks size and SHA-256 at install and only the signed record and the size at load.

properties_provided.conditions: a file from any source is installed or served onward only when its record verifies against enough trusted keys for that publisher name holding the scope its kind needs (`models` for a model, else `data`; one key for now) and the file's size and SHA-256 match. A trusted key is a built-in or added key (every scope), a successor named by a valid key statement (the scopes of the key it replaces) or a key granted by a current root (the granted scopes), and not revoked.
properties_provided.source: docs/distribution.md "Backing up and replacing the key"

properties_provided.conditions: an added publisher never replaces Lychnion's items or files, or another publisher's ids, also not by upper or lower case or by a name Windows changes (a trailing dot) or opens as a device (`NUL`), which a record may not have (`packages/lychnion_format/lib/src/record.dart:140`), and its key statements count only for its own name. In the app, Lychnion's ids and file names (the bundled packages, the bundled catalog and Lychnion's items in every checked catalog of Lychnion's) are reserved, also when not installed: an added publisher's record for one is refused from a USB stick, a followed catalog or a base, a copy installed before is not used, and Lychnion's own replaces it (`lib/download/download_store.dart:211`).
an installed item is never replaced with an older version.

a publisher key or base key becomes trusted only after the user says yes, and a base key gets fact trust only after the user compared its code with the base's screen in person (`lib/base/base_key_code.dart`); a link alone, from the QR code or a web page, only pins the key. Two exceptions come from the publisher's own statements: a successor named by a trusted key's replacement is trusted without a dialog, and a revoked publisher's new link replaces its entry after a dialog.

an answer is built only from installed guides and shows its sources; an answer whose citations do not check out carries a warning; the app never shows bare-model text as an answer: the phone answers by itself only when the model and the guides are loaded, so a failure after the model is up (the search model, indexing, a package) turns the question bar off unless a base answers, and a question that still reaches it gets a "cannot answer without the guides" message (`lib/ask/answer_rules.dart:12`).

when a hazard question matches, the fixed safety line from a Lychnion-signed package is shown word for word above the AI text; no other publisher or key supplies it: a package whose record is not valid for `safety-lines` (signed by a built-in publisher with a key holding that scope, `DownloadStore.givesSafetyLines`) is loaded without its alerts (`lib/ask/model_loading.dart`, `KnowledgePackage.withoutAlerts`), and the log says why; another publisher's copy of a bundled Lychnion package is not loaded, and Lychnion's download of one that is not valid for `safety-lines` is not used: the bundled file is, and Downloads says so (`DownloadStore.bundledPackageSource`); an empty trigger word matches nothing.

only models signed by Lychnion are installed and loaded: a `model` record from any other publisher is refused in catalogs (also followed ones and bases), on USB sticks, when installing and by nodes when they pull, and one installed by an older build is never loaded or picked (`packages/lychnion_format/lib/src/publishers.dart:21`).

with a pinned key, the phone accepts a base answer only when its Ed25519 signature covers the phone's nonce, a hash of the request and the exact body; once that base has signed, unsigned answers are refused. A QR code with `s=1` says the base signs, so unsigned answers are refused from the first one. A late answer from a previous base is ignored. An answer from a base without a pinned key, or an unsigned one, carries a note saying so.

an official or sensor fact shows as verified only with a signature from a trusted key; others count as resident reports and are labelled. Signed fields never contain control characters, so a signature never fits a different split of the fields *(maintainer, 2026-11)*.

only verified facts change the suggested evacuation site or walking route: a shelter is avoided, a road routed around and a warning's hazard used only when the fact is confirmed (`lib/map/map_state.dart:64`, `lib/map/map_state.dart:183`, `lib/map/map_state.dart:56`); unconfirmed ones are shown with their label.

a fact dated in the future, or with a lifetime far beyond normal, does not win its topic: a fact dated more than 30 minutes ahead, living longer than 3 days, or expiring more than that from now is refused on arrival and never current (`lib/facts/fact_store.dart:352`); among facts of the same trust, one dated after now loses to every one that is not (`lib/facts/fact_store.dart:384`) until its date comes, so a date in the 30-minute window can delay an override by at most that long, as a report sent at that time could.

every request has limits: 100 connections in all, 24 from one address, body 8 KiB within 10 s, question 500 characters, 8 live questions, one per address, 30 s idle, 30 s send stall, answers stop when the phone leaves. No single request makes the base hang, crash or allocate without bound. Threshold: a hang or unbounded allocation is a bug; slow under a flood is not (§1.12 `lan-availability`).

properties_provided.conditions: what a phone or node accepts is capped: 16 KiB for a base's `/info`, 1 MiB for facts and answers, 500 facts per pull and 5,000 kept, 2 MB per catalog read within 45 s, 500 key statements per list and 1000 kept (besides revocations and theft proofs). A hostile response does not crash or hang the reader, and deeply nested JSON from any of these sources is rejected *(maintainer, 2026-11)*.

the base and Share nearby are reachable only from the local Wi-Fi or hotspot: they listen only on the device's private IPv4 addresses on interfaces with a known Wi-Fi, hotspot, tethering or wired name, never on mobile data, a known VPN or virtual interface, carrier-grade NAT (100.64/10) or a public address (and on loopback, which only the device itself reaches), and follow those addresses as the network changes (`lib/base/lan_sockets.dart`).
servers answer only fixed routes and serve files only by SHA-256 from verified records or the node folder; no request part becomes a path.
the browser page shows all data as text, never as HTML.

questions leave the device only to a base the user connected to on the local network; position never leaves; release builds do not log questions, answers or position. A base address must be on the local network: a private IPv4 address, a link-local or private IPv6 address, a `.local` name, or loopback in debug builds and on desktops (`lib/base/base_link.dart:124`); a base saved by an older build is checked again when the settings load and before connecting. Release builds leave the question, answer, search query, matched sources and region out of the log, and errors keep only their type (`lib/app/dev_flags.dart:99`).

from a base or a nearby phone, the app downloads only files on that device, never from other addresses its catalog names or redirects to: the redirect guard counts as local every host that discovery and base addresses accept, from one shared definition of the private ranges (`packages/lychnion_fetch/lib/src/downloader.dart:416`), plus plain names without a dot (`packages/lychnion_fetch/lib/src/downloader.dart:430`).
a file gets its final name only after its size and hash match; on failure the last good file stays.
the plain desktop publisher key stays in the app folder and is never served or shared. The only copy that leaves it is the passphrase-encrypted backup the operator saves.
removing a publisher deletes and unloads its items.
properties_provided.source: help/en/07-publishers.md "How do I add a publisher, such as my city?"

properties_provided.conditions: a node skips file addresses on private or local networks, also after a redirect, unless the catalog itself is on such a network; an internet catalog's own redirects are checked the same way. Private or local means any address that is not plain public unicast, including `::`, multicast, special ranges and IPv4 carried in IPv6, Teredo and site-local (`packages/lychnion_node/lib/src/pull.dart:397`). DNS rebinding is not caught.

a replacement or a grant counts only when the old key signed it and the new key countersigned it, a grant only when the old key is a current root (the newest trusted key of a root's chain) and never of `keys`; a revocation only when the revoked key signed it, or a current root of the same publisher (`by`) and the revoked key is trusted through a grant, never a key of a root chain; and only when the key that made it is trusted for that publisher at that moment. A revoked key, a key with two successors, a granted key whose short id clashes with a root chain's or another granted key's, and any key reached only through them is not trusted. A root's grants lapse when it is replaced. A replaced root keeps every record scope; revoking it, or a theft conflict on it, also cuts off its successors on phones that know only the old key as built in, so a stolen root is neutralised only by an app update with new built-in roots. The current roots' statements are taken and kept first, also in catalogs, at most 100 grants, 100 revocations `by` a root and 200 root-chain replacements per publisher; revocations (by the key itself, and the roots' `by` revocations within their cap) and theft proofs have a budget of their own on phones, so no other root can crowd them out. Half of that budget is kept for the built-in publishers; added publishers' revocations and theft proofs together use at most the other half, and the halves of a theft proof that arrive together are kept together or not at all (a half that arrives after its partner is stored may not fit a full budget). This protects the built-in publishers' revocations, not one added publisher's from another's. A root's grants and revocations `by` it lapse when it is replaced, and past its cap a root cannot revoke more keys until it rotates. Builds without key scopes (lychnion/lychnion#125) ignore grants and revocations `by` another key. This holds for the `lychnion` key too.
properties_provided.source: docs/distribution.md "Backing up and replacing the key"

properties_provided.conditions: once a revocation is learned, items whose record the revoked key signed are no longer used. Their files stay on disk, and their version still blocks a downgrade.
properties_provided.source: docs/distribution.md "Backing up and replacing the key"

properties_provided.conditions: the private key in a backup is readable only with the passphrase (Argon2id, then AES-256-GCM; name and public key bound). Restore never replaces a key, never restores a key this computer knows as revoked or replaced, and writes nothing on a wrong passphrase or a damaged file.
while a computer serves phones, answers to phones and to its own Ask page never mix, and a phone that leaves stops only its own answer.

properties_not_provided.reason: Correct or complete wording of AI answers. Source and safety line are shown; stated limit, not silence
Proof that a cited passage supports the sentence. [n] means only "this passage was given to the model"
Truth of signed content, or the signer's authority over a shelter. Records, facts and answers; a signature proves origin
Vetting of an added publisher's guides, including text that steers the model, synonyms and vectors. Only under that publisher's own name; not its safety lines or models

Protection against being kept on old data. No expiry on records or key statements; catalogs unsigned; a carrier can withhold anything, a publisher status too (then only the age of the newest status seen shows); where a status is passed on, held-back versions show and its revocations and withdrawals apply; older apps ignore statements and statuses; also after delete, publisher removal, reinstall or on a fresh node
Rotation, revocation or removal of base (fact) keys. Publisher keys, Lychnion's included, have signed replacement and revocation (key-statement-verification)
Protection against the holder of an old or stolen publisher key who revokes it or names a second successor. Phones that added that key drop it and its successors until the user adds the new link

Resistance of a key backup to offline guessing of a weak passphrase; protection of the backup file where the operator keeps it. Passphrase of at least 12 characters; the operator chooses where to save
Confidentiality on the Wi-Fi of questions, answers, facts and the list of installed packages. Plain http on the local network; packages are public data

Integrity of the browser page for phones without the app. Plain http, unsigned. The page shows no current facts (shelter status, warnings) and says that it is not checked; the base's screen says so next to the page's QR code, where the Wi-Fi cannot change it (lychnion/lychnion#116). Encryption waits for #109
Protection against stripping signatures before a pinned base has signed once. Only for a QR code without s=1 (older codes), until the first signed answer; the "unsigned" note is the defence
Defence against cross-site requests and DNS rebinding from a web page. While bases run without internet; in scope again if bases are meant to have internet
Availability of a base against a device on the Wi-Fi that floods connections or questions. Per-request limits still hold (base-request-limits)
Availability of a node exposed to the internet without a reverse proxy. Unsupported setup (§1.6)
A time limit per download, or a disk quota. Size and hash still decide; a bad mirror costs time; a full disk ends a run
properties_not_provided.source: docs/distribution.md "Security", "A bad mirror costs time, not safety"; "Sync between nodes", "a full disk ends the run"

properties_not_provided.reason: Limits on which hosts a followed or main catalog sends the app to. Not for catalogs from a base or nearby phone (lan-device-same-origin)
All-or-nothing network updates of items with several files. Each file still matches a signed hash; the USB stick path is atomic
Re-checking hashes of installed files at load. Changing app files needs device control
Safety of llama.cpp, sqlite3 and map renderers on crafted files. Files from Lychnion or a trusted publisher; defects go upstream
Exclusion of app data from OS backups. The user's own backup choice
Limits on a question typed on the device. Input against the user's own device
Protection against a 48-bit key-id collision that replaces a trusted base key. Denial of service only; the attacker cannot sign as the base
That a source link's label names its destination, or that it uses https. Links from packages or bases

That a publisher "Checked by Lychnion" publishes correct or safe guides, or that one not checked is not official. An attestation says only that Lychnion checked the key belongs to the named body; labels only, never access; in a base's answers the label is the base's word
properties_not_provided.source: docs/attestations.md "What an attestation does, and what it never does"

properties_not_provided.reason: A warning for every misleading publisher name. A list of words and some look-alike letters; other names pass, still labelled "not checked by Lychnion"; never refuses. The code the user compares is 48 bits
properties_not_provided.source: docs/attestations.md "The warning for names that look official"

attack_classes: Fake facts or answers, read questions, crash or hang a base or phone
Use the base or read installed items
Get a key trusted, follow a hostile catalog, point the phone at a hostile base
Install a tampered file, hide updates, learn what users download
Install a tampered or squatting item
Replace Lychnion's items or files, make its lines look official
Impersonate the publisher, or make phones drop it
downstream_responsibilities: When the app asks, compare the key's code with the one on the body's official website before ticking it.
Run the base on a Wi-Fi you control; treat it as readable by everyone on it.
Keep the base offline while serving, or accept cross-site requests.
Save a passphrase backup of the key and keep it offline; restore only the newest backup; keep backups of replaced keys as safe as the newest one.
Check each --publisher key out of band, use a reverse proxy on the internet, pull a USB stick instead of serving it.
Give every recipient the source, also for a base.

known_misuse.pattern: running a base on guest or office Wi-Fi
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **A base on guest or office Wi-Fi.** It looks like any network will do. Others on it can read and change traffic, and client isolation often blocks phones anyway. Use a hotspot the shelter controls.
known_misuse.instead: use a hotspot or router the shelter controls

known_misuse.pattern: adding a publisher from an unknown link
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **Adding a publisher from an unknown link.** The dialog says whether Lychnion checked the publisher, but "not checked" looks harmless, and the publisher's guides then appear as answers with its name. Add only publishers you know.

known_misuse.pattern: ticking "I compared the code" without comparing
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **Ticking "I compared the code" without comparing.** For a name that looks official the tick is the last defence. Compare the code with the body's official website, or do not add it.
known_misuse.instead: compare the code with the body's official website, or do not add the publisher

known_misuse.pattern: reading "Checked by Lychnion" as "its guides are right"
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **Reading "Checked by Lychnion" as "its guides are right".** An attestation says whose key it is, not that the content is checked.
known_misuse.instead: read an attestation as whose key it is, not as a check of the content

known_misuse.pattern: treating signed as official and true
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **Treating "signed" as "official and true".** A signature says who stands behind it, not that it is right ")*.
known_misuse.instead: read a signature as who stands behind it, not as correctness

known_misuse.pattern: shipping a build with dev flags such as DEV_MENU=true
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **Shipping a build with dev flags**, for example `DEV_MENU=true` to users: it loads unchecked models.

known_misuse.pattern: serving a USB stick with lychnion_node serve
known_misuse.why_unsafe: **Serving a USB stick with `lychnion_node serve`** instead of pulling it.
known_misuse.instead: pull the stick into the node folder

known_non_findings.reported_as: Catalog urls and mirrors are unsigned, so an attacker can point downloads at their server
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers downloads, node; symptom 'integrity-bypass'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): The app or node contacts the host, and the file is installed only if its size and SHA-256 match the signed record.
known_non_findings.suppression: The app or node contacts the host, and the file is installed only if its size and SHA-256 match the signed record

known_non_findings.reported_as: Downloads from a base, phone or node use plain http, so files can be swapped
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers downloads, base-client, node; symptom 'integrity-bypass'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): Tampered bytes fail the hash and are not installed.
known_non_findings.suppression: Tampered bytes fail the hash and are not installed

known_non_findings.reported_as: The catalog keys list is unsigned, so a host can inject key statements
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers downloads, records, node; symptom 'integrity-bypass'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): The injected statements are not signed by a key the device trusts for that publisher, and are not kept.
known_non_findings.suppression: The injected statements are not signed by a key the device trusts for that publisher, and are not kept

known_non_findings.reported_as: The model gave wrong or unsafe advice
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers answers; symptom 'wrong-output'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): The answer shows its sources and the safety line where one matches; no forged citation or missing warning.
known_non_findings.suppression: The answer shows its sources and the safety line where one matches; no forged citation or missing warning
